"""Handler for capability double_entry_ledger.

Every movement in this business is a pair of postings: a debit and an equal
credit, on one date, with a narration. Nothing here stores a "balance" that
could drift -- the record IS the posting, and the answer says whether the
pair balances, what the transaction's lifecycle state is, and what the
canonical finance model made of the record.

The posting is driven through the transaction state machine (the record's
own status picks the transition), chained into the tamper-evident audit
chain, normalised and validated by the finance canonical model, and written
as a row by the database block.

Scope READS: caller input, app.models, app.money_settings (the currency is
read, never typed), the vendored blocks this capability declares.
Scope WRITES: caller output only.
Scope NEVER: no direct store write (the route owns the tenant-scoped save),
no network, no store callback, no balance column.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Dict

from app.actions._blocks import call_blocks, unavailable_field

AUTHORED_BY = "codewhale exec"

CAPABILITY_ID = "double_entry_ledger"
ENTITY = "double_entry_ledger"
BLOCK_IDS = [
    "transaction_state_machine", "audit_chain", "finance_canonical_model", "database",
]
#: Each bound block's own declared default: transaction_state_machine's
#: operation default is ``transition``; audit_chain's action default is
#: ``record_evidence``; finance_canonical_model's operation default is
#: ``schema`` and ``validate_record`` is the operation that judges a record;
#: database's action default is ``query`` and ``insert`` is the write.
BLOCK_DEFAULT_ACTIONS = {
    "transaction_state_machine": "transition",
    "audit_chain": "record_evidence",
    "finance_canonical_model": "validate_record",
    "database": "insert",
}
CAPABILITY_FIELDS = [
    "reference", "status", "entry_date", "debit_account", "credit_account",
    "amount", "narration", "transaction_ref", "posted", "reversal_of",
]

#: The database block writes to its own in-process SQLite file (HAL), not to
#: the product's ledger table: the row is the block's evidence that the
#: posting reached a database, while app/store.py holds the tenant record.
LEDGER_TABLE = "ledger_postings"

#: The lifecycle event each envelope status advances, with the actor the
#: transaction preset permits to fire it (ACTOR_RULES in the block).
_STATUS_EVENTS = {
    "open": ("post_offers", "provider"),
    "in_progress": ("accept_offer", "customer"),
    "closed": ("cancel", "system"),
}


def _number(value: Any, default: float = 0.0) -> float:
    try:
        if isinstance(value, bool) or value is None or value == "":
            return default
        return float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return default


def _currency() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """The currency the deploy declares, or a stated withholding.

    The customer owns this value (PLATFORM_CURRENCY, else the locale they
    declared), so it is read from app.money_settings -- never typed here.
    """
    from app import money_settings

    try:
        return {"currency": money_settings.currency(), "withheld": None}
    except money_settings.MoneySettingMissing as exc:
        return {"currency": None, "withheld": str(exc)}


def _period(entry_date: Any) -> str:
    text = str(entry_date or "").strip()
    return text[:7] if len(text) >= 7 else text


def analyse(payload: Dict[str, Any], money: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """What this posting is worth and whether it is a well-formed pair."""
    amount = round(_number(payload.get("amount")), 2)
    debit = str(payload.get("debit_account") or "")
    credit = str(payload.get("credit_account") or "")
    balanced = amount > 0 and bool(debit) and bool(credit)
    # Two postings to the SAME account net to nothing, which is not a
    # double entry. The record is still accepted and stored (the operator
    # has to be able to file the item and see it flagged), so this is
    # reported as a control finding, not refused at the edge.
    distinct_accounts = bool(debit) and bool(credit) and debit != credit
    return {
        "reference": str(payload.get("reference") or CAPABILITY_ID),
        "entry_date": str(payload.get("entry_date") or ""),
        "period": _period(payload.get("entry_date")),
        "debit_account": debit,
        "credit_account": credit,
        "amount": amount,
        "currency": money["currency"],
        "currency_withheld": money["withheld"],
        "balanced": balanced,
        "double_entry_ok": balanced,
        "distinct_accounts": distinct_accounts,
        "control_findings": (
            [] if distinct_accounts else ["debit and credit name the same account"]
        ),
        "narration": str(payload.get("narration") or ""),
        "transaction_ref": str(payload.get("transaction_ref") or payload.get("reference") or ""),
        "reversal_of": str(payload.get("reversal_of") or ""),
        "is_reversal": bool(str(payload.get("reversal_of") or "").strip()),
        "status": str(payload.get("status") or "open"),
    }


def _canonical_record(payload: Dict[str, Any], analysis: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """The posting in the canonical finance shape (a GL entry)."""
    return {
        "record_type": "gl_entry",
        "record_id": analysis["reference"],
        "source_system": "double_entry_ledger",
        "source_record_id": analysis["reference"],
        "transaction_date": analysis["entry_date"],
        "entity_id": _entity_id(),
        "account_id": analysis["debit_account"],
        "period": analysis["period"],
        "currency": analysis["currency"] or "",
        "amount": analysis["amount"],
        "debit": analysis["amount"],
        "credit": analysis["amount"],
        "status": analysis["status"],
        "metadata": {
            "credit_account": analysis["credit_account"],
            "narration": analysis["narration"],
            "reversal_of": analysis["reversal_of"],
        },
    }


def _entity_id() -> str:
    """The legal entity the books are kept for (an operator setting)."""
    import os

    return (os.environ.get("PLATFORM_ENTITY_ID") or "").strip() or "platform"


def _posting_message(analysis: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    unit = analysis["currency"] or "an undeclared currency"
    return (
        "posting %s: debit %s / credit %s, %s %.2f, %s"
        % (
            analysis["reference"], analysis["debit_account"],
            analysis["credit_account"], unit, analysis["amount"],
            analysis["status"],
        )
    )


def _block_inputs(payload: Dict[str, Any], analysis: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]:
    event, actor = _STATUS_EVENTS.get(analysis["status"], ("post_offers", "provider"))
    canonical = _canonical_record(payload, analysis)
    return {
        "transaction_state_machine": {
            "entity_id": analysis["reference"],
            "vertical": "transaction",
            "event": event,
            "actor": actor,
            "transition_id": "%s:%s" % (analysis["reference"], event),
        },
        "audit_chain": {
            "action_execution_id": "%s:post" % analysis["reference"],
            "action_type": "ledger_posting",
            "principal_id": "operator",
            "payload": {
                "reference": analysis["reference"],
                "debit_account": analysis["debit_account"],
                "credit_account": analysis["credit_account"],
                "amount": analysis["amount"],
            },
            "result": {"posted": analysis["balanced"], "status": analysis["status"]},
        },
        "finance_canonical_model": {
            "record": canonical,
            "record_type": "gl_entry",
            "field_map": {},
        },
        "database": {
            "table": LEDGER_TABLE,
            "values": {
                "reference": analysis["reference"],
                "entry_date": analysis["entry_date"],
                "debit_account": analysis["debit_account"],
                "credit_account": analysis["credit_account"],
                "amount": analysis["amount"],
            },
        },
    }


#: The columns the block's SQLite row carries -- declared here so the table
#: is created from the same names the insert writes.
LEDGER_COLUMNS = {
    "reference": "TEXT",
    "entry_date": "TEXT",
    "debit_account": "TEXT",
    "credit_account": "TEXT",
    "amount": "REAL",
}


def _ensure_ledger_table() -> str:
    """Create the block's table if it is not there; return a refusal or "".

    The database block owns its own HAL SQLite file and refuses an insert
    into a table nobody created ("Insert failed: no such table"). Creating it
    from the same declaration the insert writes keeps the two in step, and a
    failure here is returned as the capability's refusal -- never swallowed.
    """
    from app.actions._blocks import is_refusal, refusal_text
    from app.block_inputs import prepare_block_input
    from app.dispatch import execute

    data = prepare_block_input(
        "database", {"table": LEDGER_TABLE, "schema": LEDGER_COLUMNS},
        action="create_table", entity=ENTITY,
    )
    try:
        answer = execute("database", data, action="create_table")
    except Exception as exc:  # a block refusal is an answer, not a 500
        answer = {
            "status": "error",
            "ok": False,
            "block": "database",
            "error": "%s: %s" % (type(exc).__name__, exc),
        }
    return refusal_text("database", answer) if is_refusal(answer) else ""


def handle(payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Record the posting and answer with what it means to the books."""
    payload = dict(payload or {})
    money = _currency()
    analysis = analyse(payload, money)
    if not analysis["balanced"]:
        return {
            "ok": False,
            "capability": CAPABILITY_ID,
            "error": (
                "a double-entry posting needs two different accounts and an "
                "amount above zero (debit %r, credit %r, amount %r)"
                % (analysis["debit_account"], analysis["credit_account"], analysis["amount"])
            ),
            "analysis": analysis,
        }
    table_refusal = _ensure_ledger_table()
    if table_refusal:
        return {
            "ok": False,
            "capability": CAPABILITY_ID,
            "error": table_refusal,
            "analysis": analysis,
        }
    answers, refusals = call_blocks(
        BLOCK_IDS, BLOCK_DEFAULT_ACTIONS, _block_inputs(payload, analysis),
        entity=ENTITY, roster=BLOCK_IDS,
    )
    if refusals:
        return {
            "ok": False,
            "capability": CAPABILITY_ID,
            "error": "; ".join(refusals),
            "analysis": analysis,
            "results": answers,
        }
    return {
        "ok": True,
        "capability": CAPABILITY_ID,
        "authority": {"layer": 3, "name": "ledger_rules", "source": "app/actions/double_entry_ledger.py"},
        "analysis": analysis,
        "message": _posting_message(analysis),
        "record": payload,
        **unavailable_field(answers),
        "results": answers,
    }

]

#: The risk score at which a check must be reviewed by a person. The customer
#: owns this threshold: it is read from the deploy environment, never typed
#: into a decision here.
RISK_THRESHOLD_ENV = "KYC_RISK_THRESHOLD"
DEFAULT_RISK_THRESHOLD = 70.0

#: Where an uploaded document is looked for when the caller gives a relative
#: path (the mounted disk app/db.py resolves).
UPLOAD_DIR_ENV = "KYC_UPLOAD_DIR"
DEFAULT_UPLOAD_DIR = "uploads"


def _number(value: Any, default: float = 0.0) -> float:
    try:
        if isinstance(value, bool) or value is None or value == "":
            return default
        return float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return default


def risk_threshold() -> float:
    raw = (os.environ.get(RISK_THRESHOLD_ENV) or "").strip()
    try:
        return float(raw) if raw else DEFAULT_RISK_THRESHOLD
    except ValueError:
        return DEFAULT_RISK_THRESHOLD


def document_path(value: Any) -> str:
    """The uploaded document, if the caller's path names a real file.

    A relative path is looked for under the platform's upload directory
    first, then as given. A path that names no file is reported as "no
    document supplied" rather than handed to the OCR block, whose only
    answer for it would be that the file is missing.
    """
    text = str(value or "").strip()
    if not text:
        return ""
    candidates = [text]
    if not os.path.isabs(text):
        root = (os.environ.get(UPLOAD_DIR_ENV) or "").strip() or os.path.join(
            (os.environ.get("STORAGE_PATH") or "."), DEFAULT_UPLOAD_DIR
        )
        candidates.insert(0, os.path.join(root, text))
    for candidate in candidates:
        if os.path.isfile(candidate):
            return candidate
    return ""


def analyse(payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """What the document and the record support, before any block runs."""
    score = round(_number(payload.get("risk_score")), 2)
    threshold = risk_threshold()
    path = document_path(payload.get("image_path"))
    extracted = str(payload.get("extracted_text") or "").strip()
    decision = str(payload.get("decision") or "pending")
    reasons = []
    if not path and not extracted:
        reasons.append("no document image and no extracted text supplied")
    if score >= threshold:
        reasons.append(
            "risk score %.2f is at or above the review threshold %.2f" % (score, threshold)
        )

"""Phase gates — the checks a role must pass before the next role starts.

A gate is the only reason a long build converges instead of drifting. Each
role hands over a workspace and a claim about it; the gate is what decides
whether the claim is true, independently of anything the role said about its
own work.

Gates are values, not methods on the roles, for exactly that reason -- a
role cannot supply, weaken or skip the check that judges it. The runner
looks the gate up by phase and runs it against the workspace.

Every gate returns a :class:`GateResult` rather than raising, because a
failure is normal control flow here: it is what sends the WRITER back round
for another pass. Only a gate that cannot run at all raises.
"""

"""A platform that computes money computes it for the locale the USER declared.

FinOps (sess_065fc3eac75c4f62) was a finance platform for a Dubai business.
Its brief named no country, and the coding agent hardcoded UK VAT
(``STANDARD_VAT_RATE = 0.2``) and GBP -- so every net/VAT split it computed
was wrong for the UAE.

The locale is a typed answer, never a reading of prose:

* The Floor asks the user for a country (ISO 3166 alpha-2) and a currency
  (ISO 4217), validated by SHAPE only. They live on the session's product
  design and on the blueprint (``blueprint.locale``).
* The Factory stamps ``docs/declared_locale.json`` (the declared pair) and
  ``app/money_settings.py`` into every workspace. The settings module serves
  country / currency / tax rate at RUN time -- deploy environment first, the
  declared record second -- so no currency, country or rate is ever a value
  in Factory or generated code.
* A model declares which of its fields are money (``MONEY_FIELDS``, emitted
  from the field's declared type).

The gate (writer_contract) decides on the syntax tree:

* no money fields and no declared currency -> not applicable;
* money fields but no declared currency -> WITHHELD("no currency declared");
  never a frozen guess;
* declared -> FAIL when a module carries the declared currency or country
  code as a literal, or scales a money value by a numeric literal other than

MONEY_SETTINGS_MODULE = "app.money_settings"

_COUNTRY_SHAPE = re.compile(r"[A-Z]{2}")
_CURRENCY_SHAPE = re.compile(r"[A-Z]{3}")

#: Factors that do not change an amount's scale (identity / zeroing).
_IDENTITY_FACTORS = frozenset({0, 1})


def shaped_country(raw: Any) -> Optional[str]:
    value = str(raw or "").strip().upper()
    return value if _COUNTRY_SHAPE.fullmatch(value) else None


def shaped_currency(raw: Any) -> Optional[str]:
    value = str(raw or "").strip().upper()
    return value if _CURRENCY_SHAPE.fullmatch(value) else None


def declared_locale(country: Any, currency: Any) -> Optional[Dict[str, str]]:
    """The typed pair, or None when either is missing or mis-shaped."""
    c, cur = shaped_country(country), shaped_currency(currency)
    if not c or not cur:
        return None
    return {"country": c, "currency": cur}

    raw = blueprint.get("locale") if isinstance(blueprint, Mapping) else getattr(blueprint, "locale", None)

    return declared_locale(raw.get("country"), raw.get("currency"))

# Money Transfer Payments Platform -- deploy settings. Copy to .env and fill in.
#
#   cp .env.example .env      # .env is git-ignored and never baked into an image
#
# Nothing here has a default in the image. A setting the platform cannot run
# without fails at BOOT, naming the variable; a setting only one path needs
# refuses at the call that needs it, also by name. The values below are
# examples an operator replaces -- there is no real secret in this file.

# --- authentication -------------------------------------------------------
# REQUIRED. The platform tenant's bearer token. app/settings.py::boot_settings()
# validates it once at boot and refuses to start, naming this variable, when it
# is missing. Every /v1 route authenticates with it -- reads included.
PLATFORM_TOKEN=
# Further tenants as [redacted] pairs, comma separated. Each token resolves to
# its own tenant, and one tenant can never read another's rows.
#   TENANT_TOKENS=platform-token:local,second-tenant-[redacted]
TENANT_TOKENS=
# Optional display names for those tenants, as tenant:name pairs.
TENANT_NAMES=

# --- persistence ----------------------------------------------------------
# The single persistence root. The image declares STORAGE_PATH=/data and creates
# it owned by the unprivileged service user; /health reports the disk
# fail-closed, so a deployment that mounts its volume elsewhere answers 503
# instead of losing the ledger on the next deploy. The vendored database block's
# own SQLite file is placed here too (DATA_DIR defaults to STORAGE_PATH).
STORAGE_PATH=/data
# Optional. SET means Postgres; UNSET means SQLite at $STORAGE_PATH/platform.db.
# DATABASE_URL=[redacted]host:5432/payments

# --- money ----------------------------------------------------------------
# Country, currency and the tax rate are the customer's own values. Money paths
# read app/money_settings at the point of use and report the money leg as
# WITHHELD until they are declared -- never a guessed jurisdiction, code or rate.
# The declared locale (docs/declared_locale.json) is used when the environment
# is silent.
# PLATFORM_COUNTRY=AE
# PLATFORM_CURRENCY=AED
# PLATFORM_TAX_RATE=
# The legal entity the double-entry postings are booked to in the canonical
# finance model.
PLATFORM_ENTITY_ID=platform

# --- the business's own controls (defaults in brackets) -------------------
# Approvals: the principals the platform will take a decision from. A free-text
# approver is refused, never trusted.
APPROVED_PRINCIPALS=duty-manager,compliance-officer
# KYC: risk score at or above which a check is forced to human review.   (70)
KYC_RISK_THRESHOLD=70
# Where an uploaded ID document is looked for when the caller gives a relative
# path.                                              ($STORAGE_PATH/uploads)
KYC_UPLOAD_DIR=
# Bank reconciliation: the decimal tolerance treated as a match.      (0.01)
RECONCILIATION_TOLERANCE=0.01

# --- edge and observability ----------------------------------------------
# Request body ceiling, refused with a typed 413 before parsing.  (1048576)
REQUEST_MAX_BYTES=1048576
# Failed-authentication throttling: window in seconds, then the count.   (60/20)
AUTH_RATE_WINDOW_S=60
AUTH_RATE_MAX=20
# Optional error tracking; inert when unset.
# SENTRY_DSN=

# --- connectors this build does not configure -----------------------------
# The platform runs offline and declares no placeholder connector: these are
# named so an operator knows what a FULL deployment would supply. Without them
# the blocks that need them are reported per capability under
# "blocks_unavailable" -- never a fabricated success.
# SMTP_HOST=
# SMTP_USERNAME=
# SMTP_PASSWORD=
# KIMI_API_KEY=

```
app/main.py            FastAPI app, lifespan migrations, body ceiling, console, health, metrics

app/models.py          the single declaration: FIELDS, CONSTRAINTS, ENTITY, MONEY_FIELDS

app/block_inputs.py    shapes a domain record into what each block's own contract declares
app/store.py           SQLAlchemy Core persistence over the declared schema (from app/models.py)

app/health.py          fail-closed /health
alembic/versions/      real DDL: one op.create_table per entity (+ lifecycle audit, work queue, RAG)
vendor/                the pinned Store blocks and the runtime slice they stand on
```
